conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Music Box
style.description: The open movement of a music box, shot macro in warm bright light on pale wood: a lathe-turned brass cylinder studded with steel pins turns slowly toward a polished steel comb; each pin presses one tooth down and lets it go, the tooth springs back, rings visibly and warms in colour for a moment; a hand crank with a wooden knob drives the cylinder through a brass pinion and a worm spins a two-vane governor. One note list (tune.js) places every pin (angle around the cylinder = when, position along the axis = which tooth), moves every tooth in closed form and writes the score, one pitched bar note per pin at the exact release time. Engraved track rings and bar lines on the cylinder make it read as a score. Captions on an ivory plate with a brass edge.
motion: The cylinder turns at a constant rate (angle = omega * t); nothing else drives the picture.
A pin presses its tooth down for ~0.3 s, lets go, and the tooth rings: tip = -A exp(-s/tau) cos(2 pi f s), closed form.
A ringing tooth warms in colour for a moment, so the eye finds the note the ear hears.
Crank = 5 x the cylinder rate through a pinion; governor worm = 40 x (one turn per wheel tooth).
Camera: one short move per beat, locked during holds; macro shots sit on the line where pins meet tooth tips.

notes.mechanism: tune.js: pin angle psi = PI/2 + aRel - omega * T (T = note time), pin x = tooth x; tooth tip = min(-A exp(-s/tau) cos(2 pi f s), pin stop); cylinder angle = omega t. SCORE = one marimba + pluck per pin at T.
notes.tune: Pinwheel Lullaby (original, C-major pentatonic), 80 pins on 12 teeth, one cylinder turn = 14.6 s
notes.contact: a pin holds its tooth 0.28 s, tip travel 66 mm (toy scale), closest re-pluck 0.75 s
notes.numbers: no data shown; the visible vibration frequency (6.5-10.5 Hz) is a stand-in for the audible pitch, which would alias at 30 fps
